key_insight: MediX-R1 enables medical multimodal LLMs to produce clinically grounded, free-form answers by fine-tuning a vision-language backbone with Group-Based RL and a composite reward that enforces semantic correctness beyond multiple-choice formats.
problem_solved: Addresses the limitation of existing medical evaluation/training pipelines that rely on multiple-choice or short labels, enabling open-ended, clinically accurate responses and robust semantic evaluation of paraphrased answers.
method: Fine-tune a vision-language backbone to support multimodal clinical inputs (images + text) and free-form outputs.
Apply Group-Based Reinforcement Learning to stabilize training across diverse clinical scenarios and scale open-ended answer generation.
Use a composite reward: an LLM-based binary (YES/NO) accuracy judge for strict clinical correctness plus a medical embedding–based semantic reward to capture valid paraphrases and nuanced reasoning.
impact: Provides a practical framework for training and evaluating medical MLLMs that produce trustworthy, human-readable clinical answers—improving reliability for deployment and research on real-world diagnostic reasoning.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: vision-language backbone + Group-Based RL loop + composite reward modules (LLM judge + medical embedding).
Reward flowchart: input answer → LLM YES/NO accuracy check and embedding similarity score → combined reward.
Before/after examples: multiple-choice vs. free-form model outputs with annotations showing improved clinical correctness.
Performance chart: metrics comparing semantic correctness and clinical accuracy across baselines and MediX-R1.
paper_title: MediX-R1: Open Ended Medical Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Sahal Shaji Mullappilly, Mohammed Irfan Kurpath, Omair Mohamed, Mohamed Zidan, Fahad Khan
